items.title: John L. Jones Interview, 1972-06-05
items.q: So I never heard I mentioned Joe Oliver. Joe Oliver come from Bunshire, Louisiana.

ctx.x: Heard of him. He's still around? Yeah.

He's a Almel clerk down at the Post Office. He don't play anymore. I work with Renny and I work with Renny. He was offing and on at the La Vida when he had his brother playing drums. Joe. Joe Renny. Paul was on the saxophone or either Lexus. You ever heard of a saxophone player named Alexis? I've heard of him but I never didn't know him. He was at the La Vida then. Then Renny came over to the fund on the Budweiser. He was over there with Sporter, William Young. Sporter. He was in the Bull. Yeah.
In the Bull. Who is William Young?

items.title: John L. Jones Interview, 1972-06-05
items.q: The interviewee states 'he was with King Oliver' referring to Herman Franklin, and mentions King Oliver's death and origin, but does not claim a personal relationship with King Oliver himself.

ctx.x: I've heard him on record. How you like him? Oh, he was fine. I never heard Herman Franklin. I met him, but I never heard him.

Well, he was with King Oliver. He stayed with King Oliver until King Oliver died. He was with Celestan too for a while. Yeah, I know. He came with Celestan. He was with Celestan before King Oliver died. Now, after King Oliver died, he came back to Celestan.
He still got a little bit left on the tape. And trombone players, they haven't he got trombone players?
